And I just want to know, as the drafter of this document, how you would have come into that -- how you would have come into possession of that information.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: The drafting of this information was a result of an information that I received from the field, from a subordinate command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And to which entity was the document in front of you sent, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This information was sent to the General Staff, to the appropriate department of the General Staff, to Kakanj, among other recipients.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Which department of the General Staff, sir? Can you be a little more specific?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Such information would be sent to the Security Administration of the General Staff, to the security organ of that Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: How do you know specifically that this particular document was sent to the security organ of the General Staff? And if we could scroll up a little bit on the B/C/S version of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we do the same in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: We'd actually have to go to the first page of the English, Your Honour. I apologise for that. I should have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know -- can you tell us how you know that this document in front of you was sent to the Security Administration of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: On the document itself, on the right-hand side of it, it says: "Security Administration of the General Staff of the Army of BiH."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And what about the stamp on the document, sir, what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It indicates that this information was received in the General Staff in the Security Administration, Military Security Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 774.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P02206. If we could scroll down on the B/C/S version of the document and move to page 2 of the English language version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the initials "SS" at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And are those your initials, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Why do your initials appear on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Because I wrote this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Your Honour, I would ask now that this particular document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we able to get an explanation of the handwritten markings on the Bosnian document before we do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Spahic, there's a handwritten comment at the top of the Bosnian version of the document, and if you could explain to us what that says and, perhaps if you know, who wrote that.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It says: "Izet, I draw your attention to the seriousness of this content." In other words: "Izet, I draw attention on the seriousness of this content. Vehicles are late towards ZS-S." Possibly -- I can't read, it's illegible, the next two words. Something "blamed, because had we requested from the Ustashas on time that they return the Arabs to us, that then they wouldn't have given them to the Chetniks." And I can't recognise the signature. I can't see any signatures here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know why this particular comment was made on this document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much. Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 775.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P02204. And I just note for the record that this document is dated the 3rd of July, 1995, and that it's titled: "El Mujahedin activities on the release of the Arabs imprisoned in Kiseljak."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us how you would -- actually, let me -- if we could go to page 2 of the Bosnian version, actually. Actually, sorry, page 2 of the English version. Just scroll down on the Bosnian version. Sir, the initials "SS" appear on this document as well. Can you tell us whether or not you drafted this particular document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did, I drafted this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll up a little bit on the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us how you would have compiled the information that's in this particular document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: We would receive information on the basis of the use of technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you expand on that answer? Can you tell us, when you say, "We would receive this information on the basis of the use of technical equipment," if you can expand on why you were using this technical equipment and what information you were obtaining by the use of this technical equipment?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This piece of information was drafted on the basis of intercepted conversations, meaning wire-tapping of telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, there's a -- there's a reference to a person called "Hadzi Cengic", sir, in this document. If you could tell us, if you know, who Hadzi Cengic is?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Hadzija Cengic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, Hadzija Cengic.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: He was a logistics operative at the General Staff, as far as I know, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you know what his specific position within the General Staff was, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: He was from Logistics, and he was based in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And do you know what his full name was, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would ask now that this particular document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 776.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P02217.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, the initials "SS" appear on this document as well. Can you confirm for us whether or not you drafted this particular document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I also wrote this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if you could just briefly tell us what this document concerns.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It concerns a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment, Kasim Celenka, who drowned in a river after being wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 -- return to page 2 of the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to direct your attention to the last paragraph in this particular document, and there's only one sentence in that paragraph and it reads: "We are going to request the security organ of the El Mujahedin unit to submit a detailed report about the cause of the accident ..." And I'm wondering, sir, as the drafter of this document, how did you know that the El Mujahedin Detachment had a security organ?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I drafted this information on the basis of an information received from a subordinate unit, from the security organs of a subordinate unit. Therefore, that what was written in the security organ of a subordinate unit, that I introduced into this information which was going to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honour, I would ask now that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 777.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P02341. And if we could go to page -- actually, let me the English come up. I just note, for the record, that this document is dated the 29th of July, 1995. If we could go to page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S version of the document. And if we could possibly -- I don't know if it's possible to get the whole -- I mean, a part of the B/C/S version of the document is cut off. If it's possible to get the whole thing. It's fine like that, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the initials "SS" on this document? If we could scroll up a little bit on the English version of the document. Thanks, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I drafted this information as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask now that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 778.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P02755.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course I have no objection to this document being admitted, and for obvious reasons there is a link with the witness, but I do believe that the Defence has the right to receive information, what is the drift of the Prosecution with respect to certain documents, this document, so that we know how to organise our Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I can put a question to the witness, Your Honour. I was trying to save time. I thought the document itself was -- the relevance of it was very apparent, but I can certainly put a question, a couple of questions to the witness. If we could go back to -- actually, if we could return back to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me say this, Mr. Menon: In addition to what Madam Vidovic is saying, it's not just for them to understand the drift, but it's also for the Chamber. You know, a lot of documents are identified and, without anything being mentioned about their content, are thrown in. I'm not sure whether is it anticipated that, "Okay, fine, there are documents, go and find out what is the relevance, and do the case for the Prosecution", or, you know, it's all for the person who's tendering the document? We would also like to know what is the relevance. Actually, as she stood up, I was just inclined to ask you the same question, and I'm just getting inclined to want to refuse these documents which are just identified and tendered, when we don't know what their relevance is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, as it pertains to this document, I'll certainly put a question to the witness to identify what I believe to be relevant about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of the English version of the document and page 2 of the B/C/S version of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is now 2755?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It's -- no, actually, it's the previous exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm going to refer you to -- well, actually, let's bring up the -- it's page 3 of the English version of the document. And, sir, I'm going to refer you to the second paragraph on this particular page in front of you, and it's the third -- well, actually, it's the second paragraph on what appears on the English version in front of us. And if you could read to yourself the first sentence in that particular paragraph, and it's the second paragraph, again. Have you had a chance to read that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, in that sentence, there's a reference to losing the lines. Can you explain to us what's meant by "the lines"? What does that refer to, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: During combat activities, the lines were lost, our combat lines were lost, because -- pursuant to those reports, because of the withdrawal or the pulling out of the El Mujahedin Detachment and of the 3rd Manoeuvre and the 4th Manoeuvre Battalions from their area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, if you can tell us, why would the -- why would the pullout of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 3rd Man-Bat and the 4th Man-Bat result -- have resulted in the loss of these lines, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: As it is stated here, judging from the words of the fighters and the wounded who were there at the time of the attack, they did not know what was going on. There was a melee in the area of combat operations,. And in accordance with this, as it's stated in this document, the system of command and control completely failed, both of the brigades and the battalions concerned, because the situation was not under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But, sir, what specifically about the pullout of the El Mujahedin Detachment would have resulted in the loss of lines, if you can tell us? And tell us if you know. I mean, I don't want you to speculate.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, this did not concern just the El Mujahedin Detachment's pullout but also the pulling out of the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion and the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion, which means three units were withdrawn from their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could just go back to the first page of both the English and the B/C/S version of the document. I simply wanted to note for the record what the date of this document was, and it's the 29th of July, 1995. Your Honour, with that particular explanation, I would ask that this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Menon, what we learn here is that the El Mujahid Detachment pulled out from a certain area and that also the 3rd and the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion, I think it was, pulled out, and so for that reason the remaining forces of the -- was it the 328th Brigade -- were there left all alone on the front line and they were run down by the Serbs during an attack that ensued shortly after. Is that a correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Actually, if we could return to that particular --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could return to page 3 of the English version of the document, and page 2 of the B/C/S version of the document, and if we could scroll up on the English version of the document. Your Honour, I can certainly -- I mean, I don't want to answer that question, because then I would be testifying. I have a certain interpretation of this particular document, having examined it myself, and I'm not sure if Your Honours would want to hear that. I think Your Honours would probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't want your interpretation. We want you to tell us, through the witness, what we are supposed to make -- get the witness to tell us -- to direct us at what we are supposed to make out of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain to us -- well, let me return to the question that I had put to you previously. What -- why would the -- why would the pullout of the El Mujahedin Detachment and these two other units have resulted in the loss of these combat lines?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: The very withdrawal of those units from defence positions freed up those lines of defence, and no sufficient or adequate resistance was being offered from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know why these particular units were withdrawn from these particular lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And do you know how much terrain these particular units covered on the line of defence?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It's not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I can go much further with this witness on this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted, and it was given Exhibit 778 as the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and my -- Mr. Mundis has just indicated to me that the commander of the 328th Brigade will be appearing as a witness shortly, so he perhaps could explain that -- the significance of that particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I had asked, actually, before we return to this document, that the witness be shown Exhibit P02755. And if we could scroll down on the English version of the document just a little bit so that we get the first sentence of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to read the first sentence of this document to yourself.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, are you aware of the event that's described in the first sentence of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you became aware of this particular event?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I came to know about it from members of the military police who were present in this centre for prisoners of war in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us why the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment were given permission to visit a prisoner of war?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, I would ask now that this particular document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that in this case, the Prosecutor has failed to lay the foundation for the admission of this document into evidence. The witness doesn't know the contents of the document. He's not the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the witness said he knows about the contents of the first sentence, although I'm not quite sure whether that necessarily establishes a link. But you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's fine. The author of the document or the person whose name is listed on the signature line is going to appear as a witness. As a matter of -- just as a matter of introduction, I thought I would have the witness talk about this particular document, especially since in his statement he refers to an incident which is described in this document. But it's fine if it's marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, then the document is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 779.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And the final exhibit that I would like to have shown to this witness is P02516. If we could scroll down a little bit on the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what this particular document concerns?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This document speaks of the violent behaviour of the El Mujahedin Detachment and its members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 in the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us specifically what incidents it's referring to in respect of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Among other things, it is stated here that 20 members of the El Mujahedin Detachment took building material off various homes and took it to the village of Mehurici, near Travnik. They used the material to build a facility for their command, the Command of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir --

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Or, rather, the parent company's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, to whom was this particular document sent, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This document was sent to the Security Administration of the General Staff of the BH Army, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, are you the drafter of this document?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And how do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I know by my initials, "SS."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask now that this document be tendered into evidence, and with that I would conclude my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Menon. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 780.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That would certainly be a convenient time to take a break. We'll come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'd actually concluded my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You had concluded your leading. Thank you so much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and I will be examining you on behalf of the Defence for General Rasim Delic. You will be able to answer most of my questions with a "yes" or "no." Such is the nature of cross-examination. Please bear in mind that you should always wait for my question to be interpreted before you give an answer, because we speak the same language and this results in a confusion on the transcript. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, too. I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I will be dealing with your statement and then with the documents you commented upon. In paragraph 6 of your statement, you say that prior to the war, you worked in the State Security Service. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war and during the war, these duties were carried out within the framework of the civilian police and within the competences it had; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 of your statement, you said that you attended a one-year course within the Military Security Service in Belgrade, whereas in fact you attended a course within the State Security Service; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, during my tenure in the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This course had to do with the civilian security-related matters and not military security-related matters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before you became Deputy Commander for Security at the Training Centre in Zenica on the 20th of August, 1992, you had not had any experience in matters of military security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You assumed your duties in the 3rd Corps in early January of 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Logistics Department of the 3rd Corps, you worked until the month of February 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I've been asking you this because I have some questions for you concerning paragraph 14 of your statement, about the events in the village of Maline in 1993. You said that you had heard that members of the El Mujahedin unit had cut the throats of some individuals in Maline. You stated this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Spahic, I -- or, rather, if I suggested to you that that event happened in June of 1993, would you accept that in that case, you were far -- it was not even remotely possible for you to receive any information on this event?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not have the exact information about these events. My knowledge about these events was based on the stories rumoured around the members of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not have any knowledge of the perpetrators involved?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any accurate information on the perpetrators of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not have any knowledge of the measures taken or not taken by the Security Service of the 3rd Corps with regard to these events?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: In relation to this event and in relation to what the Military Security Service may have done, I didn't have any knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This, because at the time you worked for the Logistics Centre of the 3rd Corps, which was not even remotely close to where the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps was stationed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't receive any reports which would enable you to know whether an investigation was conducted or not?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: The security organ of the logistics base did not receive reports from the ground on these events.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I want to put some questions to you concerning the paragraphs 18 and 17 of your statement. There, you state that from February 1995, you were performing the duties of the Chief of Analysis Department, and you explained that you received reports from the security organs of subordinate units, and on the basis of the information that they provided, you prepared reports that you submitted to your superior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your superior was the Assistant Commander for Security of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the assistant commander would be the one to decide on the fate of these reports, he would be the one to decide whether to pass them on or not?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: The Assistant Commander for Security decided which information was to be forwarded and where.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also decided about the information he was going to pass on to the Corps Commander and which information he was not going to pass on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, though -- or, rather, most of the information was passed on to the commander, and he was aware of them. There were daily briefings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the Security Service could only inform the commander?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, if there was a procedure for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But they did not have the obligation to provide all the information to the commander if he was the target of their treatment? And I'm speaking of the commander of the Corps.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: There was no obligation in place to send all the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In paragraph 19 of your statement, you said that there were -- there was a rule book in your service. These were the rules governing the work of the Military Security Service; is that right? Is that right? You spoke about that?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just told us that members of the Military Security Service were subordinate to the corps commander, but will you agree with me if I say that they were responsible for the legality of their work to their superior command?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber to who you reported, as the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, and who held you responsible for the legality of your work?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: According to the chain of command, we were responsible to the Commander of the 3rd Corps and to the superior officer -- to the superior organ of the Military Security Service of the -- of the Military Security Administration, that is, of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In which situations were you held responsible? Were you reporting to the Chief of the Military Security Administration on what matters?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Mostly on the matters that were related to security matters of the entire corps and which may have had major repercussions. Also, when we had to seek authorisation to apply certain measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're referring to the special methods of covert surveillance and monitoring, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 22 of your statement, you commented -- or, rather, you said that the Assistant Commanders for Security were at each level, subordinated to their commanders, and you mentioned the General Staff in that context. I want to clarify this part of your statement. You will agree with me that the General Staff had its Security Administration. Therefore, the Staff of the Supreme Command or, rather, its commander did not have an assistant for security, rather, he had the Security Administration which had its chief; you know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At several points in your statement, you said that you sent your reports to the General Staff. When you say, "We submitted reports to the General Staff," do you also include the Security Administration of the General Staff in that context?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: When I say that we sent reports to the General Staff, this implies that we sent our reports to the Military Security Administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the Security Administration of the General Staff is not where you worked, and you don't know how they operated?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't work there and I don't know how they worked. However, if we received certain orders from them, we had to adhere to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean if you received orders from that administration, you would comply with those orders. In connection with this, I would like to ask you this: It is true, is it not, that you received orders and missions from the Military Security Administration of the General Staff on certain matters, on certain matters?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This is not known to me, because while I was in the 3rd Corps Command and as far as I can recall at this point, but I can't really remember receiving any orders from the Military Security Administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It is possible that those orders did not reach you, but your assistant -- your superior, who was the Assistant Commander for Security?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It is possible that such orders reached my superior, Assistant Commander for Security of the Corps Commander. However, my superior officer would forward such orders either to the Analysis Sector or to the Counter-Intelligence Sector or to the Staff Security Sector, depending on the matters concerned and depending on the purview of each of those departments or sectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you something that you know about for certain, and that is how your Department for Analysis and Information functioned. First of all, you drafted your information and report exclusively on the basis of information contained in reports that you received from the security organs of your immediate subordinate units; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. All written information produced in our department were drafted on the basis of written reports received from security organs of lower or subordinate commands, or possibly from the Counter-Intelligence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The gist of my question is this: Please tell me, you did not verify such information and in no way could you claim whether the facts cited in such reports were correct, accurate, or not; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: In our Analysis Department, as far as I can say, we did not conduct any verification in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you would receive such information from your subordinate units, you would inform your immediate superior, Assistant Commander for Security, about the most salient facts; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 24 of your statement, you state that only in extraordinary circumstances you would send reports to the General Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the Military Security Administration, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given that you did not verify information received from subordinate military security organs, would you accept that you forwarded sometimes unverified information?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I cannot accept that, for the reason that we, in our information, in reports, for the most part and in a section towards the end of such reports, we would inform the Military Security Administration, in other words, the General Staff, whether we had taken some actions and which, whether we were going to try to verify information, and we would be informing them again about what had gone on before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If you had available to you verified information, then you would specify that that information was verified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct. We can have verified information, reliable source, unreliable source.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In paragraph 32 of your statement, you said that you personally did not know about any problems concerning the El Mujahid unit during 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which means that you did not receive a report from the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps indicating that they had committed grave crimes, such as murder or mistreatment of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not receive any information about the problems with the El Mujahedin Detachment. If I had received them, I would have passed them on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you some documents, and I would like to put to you the following: Information reached you on transgressions of El Mujahedin. They would attack couples, they would forbid the serving of alcohol, they would attack people who would be sunbathing or bathing in the river, things concerning non-application of religious rules?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, this was hearsay. I received no verified information about these, and I did not receive anything in writing about such matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 33 of your statement, you say that the El Mujahedin Detachment was a target of processing of the Military Security Service through wire-tapping and interception of their written correspondence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned "informants" or "associates," "collaborators," which you described as Bosnians who were members of that detachment, but what I'd like to suggest to you is as follows: You, in the Analysis Department --

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, in the Analysis Department, did not know about how collection of information and intelligence was going on, because this was within the purview of the Counter-Intelligence Department?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: We people in the Analysis Department knew how information and intelligence was gathered, but we were not involved directly in the collection of such intelligence because we were analysts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew who the sources were, but you did not maintain contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I knew, if it was stated, who was the source, but I never met the sources and neither would I know their first name, family name or their identity at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Counter-Intelligence Department was headed by Mr. Vlajcic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 35 of your statement, you explained the way that you processed such information. This is what you explained?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you would receive transcripts of conversations or copies of letters from the Counter-Intelligence Department, and then you would analyse that and forward it to your superior officer, and that would be the end of your job; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I would receive from the Counter-Intelligence Department translated conversations, translated into Bosnian, so the translation of conversations, and on the basis of such translations and intelligence contained in such conversations, I would draft an information and deliver it to my immediate superior for his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 37 of your statement, you were specifically asked about the El Mujahedin Detachment and its engagement in Vozuca activities. Do you agree with me that, in effect, you do not have any personal knowledge about these events, those events at Vozuca where the El Mujahedin Detachment were reportedly engaged in terms of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I personally have no knowledge. I do not have any firsthand knowledge. My information is based on the information that I would receive from the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And in connection with this, you said: "I did not receive anything in writing, but I did hear some stories about the murder of Serbs." And you said that they even ordered Serbs to kill other Serbs. Let us clarify this, please. Do you recall saying that or stating that, please?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I said nothing was reported to me in writing, but I heard some stories that they killed some Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I do recall saying that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, in effect, this information which ended up in this statement is not something that you received in writing from your subordinate commands, any written information about murders committed by the El Mujahedin Detachment? You received no such report?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I received no reports. I received reports about killings, but not about this event. I received no event -- reports about this particular event. As I said, nothing was reported to me in writing, but I did hear some stories about them killing some Serbs. I received, in writing, information about the killings when that document was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who showed you that document? Let's clear this up. I'm asking you about your knowledge during your service during the war. Do you understand what I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: It seems that I failed to understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Witness, in paragraph 37 of your statement, asked about the El Mujahedin Detachment and their involvement in activities in the Vozuca operation, and this is what I'm discussing, you responded: "Nothing was reported to me in writing, but I heard some stories that they killed some Serbs." And now, after that, you say: "Something was shown to me." What was shown to you? What is it that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I really cannot answer anything to your question. Are you asking me about the killings of Serbs or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we show the witness his statement and the paragraph 37. That would be Exhibit 770, paragraph 37.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this section. You say: "To your question, I can confirm ..." And this is you responding to the Prosecutor: " ... That the El Mujahedin unit were engaged in combat activities during the Vozuca operation. I know that they were either part of the unit or the whole unit stationed in Vozuca. From there they would go to combat. I do not know about any problems occurring or that they were reported or took place with respect to the El Mujahid unit during or after their involvement in combat around Vozuca." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further on, you say: "Nothing was reported written to me, but I heard some stories that they killed some Serbs and that they ordered Serbs to kill other Serbs. I did not pay much attention to this." This is what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not pay much attention to this because I had not received, in writing, anything to the effect that these events took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not receive any written report?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not receive any written report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any oral reports? Did you receive any oral report? This was my next question.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not receive any oral reports either. I just heard those stories.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard those stories, but obviously you did not take them seriously; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not take them seriously because I was interested only in written information. Written reports were what interested me, because such reports, in writing, were considered by me as a valid document that they could -- that could be forwarded to my superiors, as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you had taken such information seriously, then you would have drafted a report on that or would inform some of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I would have written a report, but how valid it would be, that's a moot point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you did not do that, did you?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not discuss those stories with military police or other competent bodies of your Command?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not discuss this matter, neither with the military police nor -- well, if there were discussions, those discussions were internal discussions within our department or maybe with some colleagues from another department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone among you from the Military Security Service try to determine whether there was any truth to those stories?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This is not known to me. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you did not try to determine the veracity of such stories, and you don't know whether those stories referred to acts committed by the Arabs, generally, who were in Central Bosnia or referring to the acts of El Mujahedin Detachment members?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that there were many stories concerning the Arabs? Some glorified them, others spread most heinous stories about them; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That is correct. This is exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to turn to documents. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 666.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see here that the Security Service of the 3rd Corps sent this document on the 21st of June, 1995, to the Security Administration, a document which concerns the activities and events involving the El Mujahedin unit. First of all, let's look at page 2 of the document, which is page 4 of the English version. Do you recognise the initials?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this document? The initials seem to be yours?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to the first page of the document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the document. It mentions the person called "Mujazin" [phoen], who was travelling and lost his passport and they're speaking of various forgeries. This is page 2, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. Do you agree with me that upon reading this part of the document, you could conclude that the Arabs used several forged passports; did you have information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Based on the information contained in this report, one can see that they had several passports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The gist of my question is the following: Can we go back to page 1 of the English version. I want you to read the handwritten annotation.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I've read it. "Take care that the information about this unit is not used outside the service." I suppose it says "the service."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this means, "take care that the information about this unit is not used outside the service"?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: To my mind, it means that the information should not be disseminated to persons who are not part of the service, that the information should be kept within the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, within the Service of Military Security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you said it's Exhibit 666.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, I'm sorry. Yes, it is. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 772.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've already seen this document today. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: One would conclude, on the basis of this document, that on the 11th of August, 1995, your service, that's to say the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, gave its approval to Izudin Besic and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: ... that it is issuing them with passports?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, our service was giving the approval for the issuance of passports to Izudin Besic and Anwar El Sajed Mohamad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that's on the 11th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 11th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put the document away. Can the witness be shown D619. In the meantime, please keep in mind the date, the 11th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo, from the Department for Administrative and General Affairs, dated the 5th of June, 1995, sent to the Security Services Centre, Zenica, signed by Zlatan Dzenanovic, chief of the department. Please look at the text. Below subject -- well, the subject says: "Delivery of the decision granting citizenship ...," and it states here: "We hereby send you the decision granting BH citizenship to Anwar El Sajed Mohamed from Egypt." Do you agree this is the same person whose name we saw in the document dated the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: The 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of 1995. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you an answer, an unequivocal answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can you place this exhibit -- can this exhibit be placed on the ELMO, because I want this name to be clearly seen in the document that the Prosecutor showed the witness today. Or perhaps I might have a better version with me. Perhaps this one is better [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the name "Anwar El Sajed Mohamed." Can it be zoomed in on? Thank you. "Izudin Besic" and "Anwar" -- could you position the document so we see the entire name? Could we also see the rest of the document? That's fine. Do you see that it says "Anwar El Sajed Mohamed"?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I can't see "El Sajed," but I do see "Anwar."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you see "Mohamed"?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I see "Mohamed," although the letter "m" is missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But would you accept nevertheless that it's the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Some of us are blind, we don't see anything. I'm trying to look, and I understand that this is a B/C/S document. Which one is "Anwar"? Is that "Anwar"? Very faint. And then where is "Mohamed"? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have "Izudin" behind "Anwar." It's just that it's not quite visible on the ELMO. I saw better copies of this document. We have "Anwar" and then "El." You can see the letter "E" at the very end. Could you move the document to the left a bit, Madam Usher. Thank you. We can see the letter "L," and we can only barely make out the letter "S."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Assuming that this is the same person, Witness, would you have -- could you in any way explain why an inquiry is sent about this person to your administration when already in the month of June 1995 it is stated that the person is in possession of a passport? Can you account for this?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I cannot account for that, and I cannot even be sure that this is one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, can this document be admitted -- or, rather, can it be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 781.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the OTP if they have a better-quality copy of this document, to send it to us. We should also like to have the original of the document, E772.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, assuming that a person has already been issued with a passport, then there's no reason for the Military Security Administration to give their position as to whether the person should be issued with a passport or not?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: If somebody already has a passport, then there's no need for that person to ask for a new passport to be issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What happened when the one passport has either expired or is full, that one has to go and apply for a new one, or this never happens in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, if a passport has expired, then one asks for a new one. However, if the passport has not expired, then there is no need for an application for a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, do you agree that the application must clearly state whether an extension of the passport is asked for or for a new one?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This document clearly shows that they are asking for a renewal of the existing passport.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, that they are not asking for a renewal but for a new passport.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said exactly the opposite of what was reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just said that this document clearly shows that they are asking for the issuing of a new passport and not for a renewal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Evidently this has been misinterpreted, yes. I said precisely what you just said. They are asking for a new passport to be issued, not for a renewal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't really remember. In countries where you cannot renew an old passport, you have to ask for a new one. Is it the same thing in your country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in our country a passport is issued for a fixed term, and it normally states the date of expiry. Normally, as far as I am aware, a passport is issued for a period of five years, at the expiry of which a new passport must be applied for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How is the application for that new one couched? Is it couched as an application for a renewal or is it couched as an application for a new passport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one can apply for a renewal, in which case the passport will bear a statement that it has been renewed, and it will also state the period by which it has been renewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand you to mean --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if one asks for a new -- one applies for a new passport, then the person will be issued with a new copy of a passport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, which you were part of, you did not work on these cases, rather it was within the remit of the lawyer within the 3rd Corps? And I'm referring to passports.

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: After a security clearance was obtained, after vetting, an officer from the Legal Affairs Department would be charged with dealing with these matters. The passport itself was issued by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. The lawyer responded to these applications and forwarded them to the police, the Ministry of the Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: We would receive an application for a passport to be issued. After we completed the security screening, we would state that a -- the given person can be issued with a passport. In this case, the person -- the member of the El Mujahedin Detachment went to the police, where he received the passport. Our department did not issue passports. This was not their job. This was the duty of individuals from the unit in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that one of the rare issues on which the El Mujahedin Detachment members would turn to the organ of the 3rd Corps would be precisely these passports?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I know that these -- this was one of the first instances when they turned to them. I don't know about the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This means that you did not come across any other such requests or applications?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now I'd like you to see another document, P2173. Can we show page 2 -- or, rather, can we show the document in such a way that the signature block is visible. Do you recognise your initials, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at paragraph 2 of this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of -- yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this document discusses the fact that Bosniak young men in the El Mujahedin Detachment were incentivised [sic] by money and that they were given food?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I do agree. I think that the young men who were engaged in the El Mujahedin Detachment received some rations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment or from the officers in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Then please take a look at paragraph 3 of this document, the latter part of paragraph 3. And that would be page 2, Your Honours, the first sentence on page 2. Witness, in the third paragraph it is written, the last sentence of the third paragraph, you also told Abu Musif that [indiscernible] Al Misri came and left behind 79.000 Deutsche marks, and that he presumes that a portion of that amount was given to the El Zubeir's group. In connection with this, I would like to ask you, because you authored this document and I presume that this information resulted from intelligence that your service obtained through intercepted conversations, please, did you know that -- did you receive intelligence that autonomously from the El Mujahedin Detachment there was a group under the name of "Abu Zubeir"?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This was not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive such intelligence or information?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you the author of this text?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This information was drafted on the basis, as can be seen, on the basis of an intercepted conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can confirm the authenticity of this information?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is authentic information, but whether the claims therein are accurate, that I cannot --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a very fair answer. Your Honours, please, if this document can be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 782.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may P2176 be shown to the witness, please. And for the record, this is a document of the Military Security Service Department of the 3rd Corps, dated 21st of June, 1995, concerning the El Mujahedin Detachment Intelligence. Could we scroll down the document so that we see the signature block.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document that I drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now please take a look at paragraph 2 of this document. It discusses some intelligence concerning activities of the El Mujahedin Detachment members. Please focus on the sentence: "In a conversation of E. Ejub ..." Ejub wanted to know where E. Jetam informed him that he was in Tuzla group, that the emir was Hubajb [phoen], and that the Tuzla group belongs to the group of El Zubeir. Where did you get this information and who drafted?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This is the information that I drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May the document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, given that you were involved in analysis, as far as I could grasp, in your documents Abu Zubeir's group and the El Mujahedin group are being both mentioned. Please tell us -- tell us, did you have information that it was possible for our units to tell those groups apart when it came to incidents?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just -- what do you mean by "our units," ma'am, if that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, thank you, Your Honours. Of course, I did not -- I said, "How was it possible to make a distinction between the El Zubeir and El Mujahedin Detachments," and of course I never said "our unit." I will repeat my question. Your Honours, I asked whether you had information, whether it was possible, and I meant the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps, to tell those groups of Arabs apart, those groups who were involved in incidents. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, you tried to answer. Can you answer right now, please?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This is not known to me. However, units out on the field from subordinate commands, where combat activities were taking place and where they did take place, and where units are stationed, given that they were there on the ground every day, they were supposed to be distinguished.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's your assumption?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I said this is my assumption, but I said that I did not personally know, and I personally did not know the distinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very well. Now I would like the witness to be shown document 21 -- P2180.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, do you agree that this is an information coming from the Military Security Department, dated 22nd of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It concerns the preparations for the start of Islamic school in the El Mujahedin Detachment. Now, could we please show the document so that the signature block is visible. Thank you. Witness, do you agree that you authored this document as well?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down the Bosnian version, please. I would like the witness to be able to see the annotation on page 1. Page 1 of the Bosnian version, please, and the English version as well. And could you focus the handwritten note on the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you read this note?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: "Use exclusively in operative work; not to be used -- this data not to be used outside of the service."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is this supposed to mean, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This means that monitoring, surveillance and collection of information should be continued, meaning the information on the work of the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Would I be right in understanding this document if I were to say that this note means that this information should not be made known outside the Military Security Service?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: This was not necessary, because it concerns the establishment of a school, and you stated this well, and this intelligence from this report should not be used outside the service and that they should be used exclusively for operative work.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you. May I tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 784.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, why is it relevant to learn about the establishment of a school? I suppose it's a school for young students, not for soldiers. Right? But what relevance does this have to the indictment? Can you clarify or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the contents of this document are not material. For the Defence, what is material is the handwritten note to the effect that documents with certain contents should be kept within the service and not to be disseminated outside the service. But this is not school for children. Unfortunately, this is a school for soldiers, Your Honours. It discusses young men and the intake of young men into this Islamic school. Maybe we can take a look at the English version so that we see how it's translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. The document was not shown on the screen long enough for me to catch that this was a school for the soldiers, but so be it. What is the significance of this information having to be kept within the security services?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this point this is a very delicate issue for me to elaborate upon at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I hope to be, well, what do I say, wiser about this matter later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honours. I don't recall whether this document has been given an exhibit number. It has.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that we'll be able to see the document P775 -- correction, that is Exhibit 775. I withdraw this, Your Honours. We've already seen it. 774, 774.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecutor recently showed you this document. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He quoted a small portion of this document, a section which says: "On that occasion, El Mujahedin Detachment's members stated that the basic goal of their struggle was to destroy the Croats and the Serbs." This is what he told you. Do you agree that it also reads that they expect all Muslims to be on Allah's path, and that because of the differences, conflicts will arise sooner or later between those units, and that the Efendi Seric is a key author. Do you know who this Mr. Seric is?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Efendi Seric is the leader of the Islamic community in Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This "Kjafir" means "the Devil"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this information contains a piece of information that the Army of BiH's struggle is being negated, they expressed their lack of acceptance of President Izetbegovic, the flag and the Commander of Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I agree, and this is how it's written.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the only information of that sort that you received?

utterances.speaker: SALIH SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know about anything else. If I were to see them, maybe I would be reminded of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This document can be put away. I have only a handful of other questions, Your Honours, but I'm mentioning this because it's 7.00, and tomorrow I will have only a few questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the end for today?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, you are -- we are not finished with your testimony. If you can come back here tomorrow at 9.00 in this same court, 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Court adjourned to 9.00 tomorrow morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
